approved: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let the environment minister ban a fishing activity while an expert panel studies its environmental effects.
It restores powers that let the minister, together with the fisheries minister, temporarily or permanently declare a fishing activity as needing assessment and prohibition.
A final declaration can last no longer than 24 months, and the minister must consider written submissions from affected fishing concession holders before making one.
Repeals a sunset provision in the EPBC Act.
Allows the minister to set up an independent expert panel to assess a declared commercial fishing activity.
Creates civil penalties and offences for carrying out a declared commercial fishing activity.
Requires the expert panel's report to be published and tabled in Parliament.
Commercial fishers and fishing concession holders who may be affected by a declaration.
